title: What If Earth Always Showed One Face to the Sun?

scenes.text: What if Earth stopped turning, so one side always faced the Sun? Half the planet could freeze.
Tidal locking is real. A star's gravity can slow a planet's spin until it matches its orbit.
One side gets permanent daylight, the other endless night. A single day would last a full year.
Models of such planets suggest the dayside can scorch, while the nightside is covered in ice and glaciers.
In models, water freezes first along the twilight line, while open ocean survives under the Sun.
Only the twilight band might stay mild. Planet scientists call these eyeball planets: life, if any, in permanent sunset.

description:
What if Earth always showed one face to the Sun?
Models of tidally locked planets suggest a scorched dayside, a frozen nightside, and a narrow twilight band between them.
